title: Compare and Contrast
objectives: I can tell how two things are alike and how they are different.
I can use similar, alike, unlike, and contrast when I compare.
I can use both, either, neither, and than in a sentence.
I can fill in a two-circle chart and say what it shows.
rationale: Comparing is the main thinking skill of second grade, and children need exact words to say it. The eight words split into how things are the same (similar, alike, both), how they are different (unlike, contrast, than), and choices between two things (either, neither). Children practice with real pairs such as a cat and a dog or summer and winter, and they build a two-circle chart that they can use again in reading, math, and science.

words.def: Almost the same, but not exactly.
words.ex: A cat and a lion have similar faces.
words.ex2: My coat and Rosa's coat are similar in color.
words.nonExample: A fish and a bird are not similar in how they move.

apps.academic: Similar shapes can be different sizes.
apps.writing: Use similar when two things share some features but are not the same.

cloze.s: The twins look so ___ that people mix them up.

cloze2.s: A frog and a toad are ___ animals, but a toad has drier, bumpier skin.

misuse.s: A tiny ant and a huge elephant are similar in size.
misuse.why: Similar means almost the same, and an ant and an elephant are very different in size.

visual.alt: A house cat and a lion facing each other.

words.def: Looking or being the same as each other.
words.ex: The two puppies look so alike that I cannot tell them apart.
words.ex2: Our two kites are alike; each one is red with a long tail.
words.nonExample: A big dog and a tiny mouse are not alike in size.

apps.academic: List how two things are alike in the middle of a chart.
apps.writing: Use alike after the things you compare: the twins are alike.

cloze.s: The two shirts are so ___ that nobody knows whose is whose.

cloze2.s: Sam and his brother are ___; they have curly hair and green eyes.

misuse.s: A snowman and a campfire are alike because one is cold and one is hot.
misuse.why: Alike means the same, and cold and hot are different.

words.def: Not the same as; different from.
words.ex: Unlike a fish, a bird has feathers.
words.ex2: Unlike my sister, I do not like spicy food.

apps.academic: Unlike a frog, a lizard has dry skin.
apps.spoken: Unlike you, I like cold weather.
apps.writing: Start a sentence with unlike to show a difference.

cloze.s: ___ a rabbit, a turtle has a hard shell on its back.

cloze2.s: ___ her brother, Lia loves to wake up early in the morning.

misuse.s: Unlike a robin, a robin has two wings.
misuse.why: Unlike compares two different things, and a robin cannot be unlike itself.

visual.alt: A turtle with a shell next to a rabbit with long ears.

words.def: To tell how two things are different.
words.ex: Mia contrasted summer with winter in her paper.
words.ex2: Please contrast a bike and a car in your answer.
words.nonExample: Saying how two things match is not contrasting them.

apps.academic: Contrast two animals by telling what each one can do.
apps.spoken: Let us contrast these two books.
apps.writing: Contrast two characters by showing one difference.

cloze.s: In class we will ___ a frog and a fish to see how they differ.

cloze2.s: She wrote a paragraph to ___ the sunny beach with the snowy mountain.

misuse.s: To contrast two shoes, tell all the ways they are exactly the same.
misuse.why: To contrast is to tell how two things are different, not the same.

visual.alt: A frog and a fish side by side.

words.def: The two together; the one and the other.
words.ex: Both of my shoes are muddy.
words.ex2: Mom and Dad both like to hike.

apps.academic: Both circles in the middle of the chart show what is the same.
apps.spoken: Both of us have a sister.
apps.writing: Use both for exactly two things.

cloze.s: I have two cats, and ___ of them love to nap in the sun.

cloze2.s: The twins are wearing blue, and ___ have new shoes.

misuse.s: I ate both of the three cookies on the plate.
misuse.why: Both means the two together, so it cannot name three cookies.

visual.alt: A pair of mittens, one for each hand.

words.def: One or the other of two choices.
words.ex: You may have either an apple or a pear.
words.ex2: Either Sam or Mia will feed the fish today.

apps.academic: Either choice will work for this problem.
apps.spoken: Either day is fine for me.
apps.writing: Use either with or to give two choices.

cloze.s: You can ___ walk to school or ride the bus with your friends.

cloze2.s: ___ the red hat or the blue hat will keep you warm in the snow.

misuse.s: You can have either one snack or all of the snacks at once.
misuse.why: Either means one choice of two, not everything at once.

visual.alt: An apple and a pear side by side.

words.def: Not one and not the other.
words.ex: Neither my cat nor my dog likes baths.
words.ex2: Neither bus came on time this morning.

apps.spoken: Neither of us wants to leave.
apps.writing: Use neither with nor to say that two things are both not true.

cloze.s: ___ the cat nor the dog wanted to take a bath in the cold water.

cloze2.s: I like ___ peas nor beans, so please give me corn.

misuse.s: Neither Mia nor Ben came to the party, so both of them were there.
misuse.why: Neither means not one and not the other, so both could not be there.

visual.alt: A cat with a red X over it.

words.def: Word used to compare two things.
words.ex: A giraffe is taller than a horse.
words.ex2: I ran faster than my brother in the race.

apps.academic: Use than with words like taller, shorter, and bigger.
apps.spoken: This book is longer than that one.
apps.writing: Write a comparing sentence with an ending such as -er and than.

cloze.s: A feather is lighter ___ a rock, so it floats on the wind.

cloze2.s: Our dog is bigger ___ our cat, but the cat is faster.

misuse.s: A mouse is bigger than an elephant.
misuse.why: Than compares two things, but this comparison is false because an elephant is bigger.

visual.alt: A tall giraffe next to a shorter horse.

passage.title: Cats and Dogs
paras: Let us contrast cats and dogs. They are alike in some ways. Both are furry pets, and both can learn tricks. Their paws are even similar.
Unlike a dog, a cat can climb a tall tree, but a dog is usually bigger than a cat. You may pick either one, but neither can talk.

qs.q: What does "contrast" mean in the first sentence?
qs.why: To contrast means to tell how two things are different.

qs.q: How are a cat and a dog alike?
choices: Both are bigger than a horse.
qs.why: The story says both are furry pets and both can learn tricks.

choices: A cat is bigger than a dog.
A dog climbs a tall tree better than a cat.
A dog is usually bigger than a cat.
qs.why: The story says a dog is usually bigger than a cat.

write.prompt: Write two sentences about how two animals you know are alike and different.
write.frame: ___ and ___ are alike because ___. Unlike ___, ___ can ___.

study.task: Draw two circles that overlap. Write two things you want to compare, one on each side. Put what is different on the outside and what is alike in the middle. Tell a partner one sentence using both or unlike.

sentences: Write a sentence about two animals that are similar.
Write a sentence that tells how you are unlike a friend.
Write a sentence about two things and use than to tell which one is bigger.

combine.model: Unlike a frog, a toad lives on land.
Both the cat and the dog like milk.

discuss: What two things in our classroom are alike? How are they different?
When do you use neither? When do you use either?
produce.explain: Explain how alike and unlike are opposites. Give one example of each.

argue.prompt: Which is more fun, summer or winter? Pick one and use than in your reason.
argue.frame: I think ___ is more fun than ___ because ___.

constructed.prompt: Pick two animals. Tell one way they are similar and one way one is unlike the other.
constructed.model: A cat and a dog are similar because both have fur. Unlike a dog, a cat can climb a tall tree.

constructed.prompt: Write two sentences about a pencil and a crayon. Use both in one and than in the other.
constructed.model: Both a pencil and a crayon can draw. A pencil is thinner than a crayon.

teacher.overview: Children learn eight words that state how two things are alike and different, and use them with a two-circle chart. Compare real objects first, then pictures, then characters. Revisit instead, wise, and foolish by comparing two choices.

notes.va.similar.adj: Similar means almost the same, alike means the same in some way. Use two leaves from the same tree. Children often say same for similar; model almost the same.
notes.va.alike.adj: Alike follows the things compared: the twins are alike. It does not go before a noun. Show with a pair of socks and a pair of shoes.
notes.va.unlike.prep: Unlike starts a sentence that shows a difference. It is not the same as dislike. Teach the prefix un- only as meaning not, as in unlike and unkind from grade 1.
notes.va.contrast.v: Contrast here is a verb: to tell how things are different. Use a two-circle chart and focus on the outside parts. Spanish speakers have the cognate contrastar.
notes.va.both.pron: Both means two together and needs exactly two things. Act out with two children and a ball each.
notes.va.either.conj: Either gives two choices, usually with or. Use a real choice, such as an apple or a pear. Keep pronunciation EE-ther; EYE-ther is also correct.
notes.va.neither.conj: Neither means not one and not the other, usually with nor. Children may say neither with a negative; model neither of us likes it.
notes.va.than.conj: Than compares two things after an -er word. Children often write then. Show both words side by side and read aloud the difference. Use real pairs such as a pencil and a marker.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I want to compare a cat and a dog. Both are furry pets, so that goes in the middle. Unlike a dog, a cat can climb a tree, so that goes on the cat side. A dog is bigger than a cat, so that goes on the dog side.'
discuss: What two things would you compare to teach a new student about our school?
Can two things be alike in one way and unlike in another way?
misconceptions: Children may use then for than. Say both words and point to the meaning.
Some children think alike and similar are the same. Similar means almost the same.
Children may use both for more than two things.
extend: Compare two characters from a read-aloud with a two-circle chart.
Write a class book called Alike and Unlike with a page for each pair.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit instead, wise, and foolish: compare a wise choice and a foolish choice for the same problem, and tell what a character did instead.

wida.oral: Pick two objects. Tell your partner one way they are alike and one way they are different, then switch.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (similar, parecidos, a diferencia de, contrastar, ambos, uno u otro, ni uno ni otro, que) not reviewed by a native speaker; function words have more than one Spanish form.
Facts checked: a toad has drier, bumpier skin than a frog; cats climb trees better than most dogs; dogs are usually larger than cats.
